question:
A coherent, collimated electron beam is accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V$ and then incident normally on a Young’s double-slit arrangement.

Each slit has finite width $a=0.10\,\text{mm}$ and the slit separation (center-to-center) is $d=0.50\,\text{mm}$. A screen is placed at distance $D=1.0\,\text{m}$.

Because of the finite slit width, the interference fringes are modulated by the single-slit diffraction envelope. It is observed that the **first missing bright fringe** (i.e. the smallest $y>0$ at which an interference maximum is suppressed due to coincidence with a diffraction minimum) occurs at a distance $y_0=1.0\,\mu\text{m}$ from the central bright fringe.

Assume small-angle approximation ($\sin\theta\approx\tan\theta\approx y/D$). Use the conditions
$$\text{Interference maxima:}\quad d\sin\theta=m\lambda,$$
$$\text{Single-slit minima:}\quad a\sin\theta=p\lambda,$$
and the non-relativistic de Broglie relation
$$\lambda(\text{in Å})=\frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V(\text{in V})}}.$$

Find the accelerating potential $V$.
